extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, Licensing & Review staff, patent applicants, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing confidentiality, access, screening, issuance, handling, and modification of Secrecy Orders and access to international patent application files (PCT) in the U.S. patent system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to international application by third parties (PCT Article 30(2)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: No national Office shall allow access to the international application by third parties unless requested or authorized by the applicant, before the earliest of: (i) date of international publication of the international application; (ii) date of receipt of the communication of the international application under Article 20; (iii) date of receipt of a copy of the international application under Article 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: a national Office may inform third parties that it has been designated or publish that fact but only limited data (receiving Office identification, applicant name, international filing date, application number, title). A designated Office may allow access for purposes of judicial authorities. 'Access' covers any means by which third parties may acquire cognizance (individual communication or general publication), but no Office shall generally publish an international application or its translation before international publication or, if publication hasn't occurred by 20 months from priority date, before 20 months from priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential nature of the international preliminary examination (PCT Article 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the International Bureau nor the International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) shall, unless requested or authorized by the applicant, allow access to the file of the international preliminary examination by any person or authority at any time, except by the elected Offices once the international preliminary examination report (IPER) has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to limited provisions (Articles 36(1) and (3), 37(3)(b)), the International Bureau and IPEA shall not give information on issuance/non-issuance of an IPER or on withdrawal/non-withdrawal of the demand or any election unless authorized by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy obligations for international applications filed in the PTO (35 U.S.C. 368)
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed in the Patent and Trademark Office are subject to Chapter 17 provisions; filing an international application in a foreign country on an invention made in the U.S. is considered filing in a foreign country within Chapter 17. If a license to file abroad is refused or an international application is ordered to be kept secret and a permit refused, the PTO acting as a Receiving Office, International Searching Authority, or IPEA may not disclose the contents to unauthorized persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acting in those capacities, the Office must withhold disclosure consistent with the statute and the PCT obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.14(g) — Conditions for furnishing copies/access to international application files
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of international application files designating the U.S. and published under PCT Article 21(2) (or copies of documents in such files) will be furnished in accordance with PCT Articles 30 and 38 and PCT Rules 94.2 and 94.3 upon written request showing publication and U.S. designation and payment of appropriate fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: Home Copy copies provided when filed with U.S. Receiving Office; Search Copy copies provided when the U.S. acted as ISA (written opinion not available until 30 months from priority date); Examination Copy access limited — only when U.S. acted as IPEA, IPER has issued, and U.S. was elected. Copies of English translations filed under 35 U.S.C. 154(d)(4) are available upon request. Requests should preferably include the front page of the published international application, be sent to International Patent Legal Administration, and include the appropriate fee. Examination Copy access is not permitted in accordance with PCT Article 38 unless conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening of applications for national security and foreign filing license (35 U.S.C. 181 and related provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: All provisional, nonprovisional, international patent applications, and international design applications in the USPTO are reviewed for the purposes of issuance of a foreign filing license; are screened upon receipt for subject matter that, if disclosed, might impact national security; and are referred to appropriate agencies for consideration of restrictions on disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional applications filed in a foreign language may require an English abstract for screening; applicants are strongly recommended to file an English description to avoid delays. Screening also identifies inventions where DOE or NASA may have property rights and processes foreign filing license petitions under 37 CFR 5.12(a). If a defense agency concludes disclosure would be detrimental, a secrecy order is recommended to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and effects of Secrecy Orders (37 CFR 5.2, 5.3; 35 U.S.C. 181)
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified by a chief officer of a defense agency that publication or disclosure would be detrimental to national security, the Commissioner will issue an order that the invention be kept secret and will withhold publication or grant for the period the national interest requires. Applications under secrecy order are processed up to specified points but publication, grant, and certain transmissions are withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational effects: national applications under secrecy order with final rejection must be appealed or prosecuted to avoid abandonment; appeals must be completed but hearings generally will not be set until secrecy order removed; interferences/derivations will not be instituted while under secrecy order; when in condition for allowance except for secrecy order the applicant and agency are notified and the application is suspended until order removal. International applications under secrecy order will not be transmitted to international authorities or the applicant and may be considered withdrawn under PCT Rule 22.3 (but U.S. filing date can sometimes be preserved by meeting 35 U.S.C. 371(c) requirements before withdrawal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Secrecy Orders (Type I, II, III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three types of Secrecy Orders of different scope: (A) Type I — Secrecy Order and Permit for Foreign Filing in Certain Countries (for critical military/space tech; lists reciprocal countries); (B) Type II — Secrecy Order and Permit for Disclosing Classified Information (for data properly classifiable under security guideline where owner has DoD Security Agreement, DD Form 441); (C) Type III — General Secrecy Order (used where other types don't apply, including orders by agencies other than DoD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type I permits the widest utilization while controlling unlawful exportation and identifies countries where corresponding applications may be filed (reciprocal security agreements). Type II treats the patent application as classified material and includes a notification of classification level. Type III prevents disclosure to anyone without express written consent but may include permits (e.g., 'Permit A') that relax restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope across related subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy Orders apply to the subject matter of the invention, not merely the patent application; other patent applications already filed or later filed which contain any significant part of the subject matter also fall within the scope of the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such related applications must be promptly brought to the attention of Licensing & Review if not already under a Secrecy Order. Effects of the Order are detailed in the notifying letter and include restrictions on disclosure and delay of any patent grant until rescission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and correspondence requirements for applications under Secrecy Order or bearing national security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications subject to Secrecy Order will be deleted from USPTO image file systems, converted to paper, held with Licensing & Review, and transferred to an examiner designated by Licensing & Review. National security classified documents must be hand-carried or mailed in compliance with specified procedures and may be filed via SIPRNET as permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All correspondence directly related to subject matter must be transmitted to prevent unauthorized disclosure (fax not permitted). Papers bearing national security markings must be referred to Licensing & Review for clarification. Authorized security markings may be placed on drawings provided markings are outside illustrations and removed when material is declassified. When changing power of attorney in an application under Secrecy Order, the applicant must provide a statement that the new attorney(s) has been apprised of the Secrecy Order. For national security classified applications, a DoD CAGE code is required to show ability to accept/store classified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rescission or modification of Secrecy Order; permit to disclose or file abroad (37 CFR 5.4, 5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any principal affected may file a petition for rescission or removal of a secrecy order (may be letter form, duplicate). Petitions must recite facts that render the order ineffectual (including complete data and copies if prior publications/patents are alleged) and identify any government contracts related to the subject matter. Petitions for permit or modification must fully recite reason/purpose and identify proposed disclosees, countries for filing abroad, and vouch for loyalty/integrity and clearance status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is denied, appeal to the Secretary of Commerce under 35 U.S.C. 181 may be taken within 60 days from denial. For permits seeking disclosure to cleared persons, adequate explanation of clearance (agency, date, degree) should be given. Organizations may petition for a general permit for repeated routine operations, ordinarily reciting the security clearance status sufficient for highest classification involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper or inadvertent disclosure reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If, prior to or after issuance of a Secrecy Order, any significant part of the subject matter or material information relevant to the application has been revealed to any U.S. citizen in the United States, the principals must promptly inform that person of the Secrecy Order and the penalties for improper disclosure. If disclosed to any person in a foreign country or a foreign national in the U.S., the principals must not inform that person of the Secrecy Order but must promptly furnish details to Mail Stop L&R for Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information to furnish includes date of disclosure; name and address of disclosee; identification of subject matter; any authorization by a U.S. government agency to export such subject matter; and identification of any foreign patent application or patent containing the subject matter, to the extent not already furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal of Secrecy Orders (35 U.S.C. 181)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Secrecy Order remains in effect for 1 year from its date of issuance and may be renewed for additional periods not more than 1 year upon notice by a government agency that the national interest so requires. The applicant is notified of any such renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiration or failure to renew does not lessen the principals' responsibility for the security of the subject matter if it remains subject to Executive Order or statutory classified information regimes unless the principals have been expressly notified that the subject patent application has been declassified and security markings may be canceled or removed.
